- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model typically peaks 1–2 days after true price peak; shift forecast peak forward by 1–2 days if sentiment is trending.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to “stick” to prior trend; force a 1–2% mean-reversion correction toward 30-day moving average of recent 7–14 days.
- When sentiment is consistently high (e.g., 0.67+ for 3+ days), model overweights short-term momentum; reduce forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment spikes by 20–30%.
